title: Turbine Channel
protagonist: Dana Okafor, marine energy siting engineer, regional utility tidal-power pilot program
primary_metric: kilowatt-hours of generation potential per cubic meter of water actually moved through the channel's cross-section, per tidal cycle

options.A: Recommend the Narrows -- a narrow, fast tidal channel with high peak current speed but a short, sharply-peaked flow window each cycle
options.B: Recommend the Reach -- a wider, slower channel with a longer, flatter flow window

scenario_constructions: Dana Okafor and the utility's tidal-power pilot program are fictional, invented for this case -- consistent with the corpus convention used for e.g. Rosa Delgado / the Fermenter case and Priya Nakamura / FlowState.

The lease-option window's remaining length (Background) is set to 12 days -- a scenario detail with no real citable source, consistent with the Overview's 'recommendation by Friday' urgency, disclosed as a stated scenario detail rather than sourced externally.

The Narrows and the Reach are fictional channels explicitly modeled on two real NOAA current stations' real published data (ca0101 and cb0102, see sources S1/S2) -- the fictional channel names/geography are invented, but the current-speed time series driving every downstream calculation is real, live-fetched NOAA data, not invented.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: The Reach's channel width at the proposed array site
modeling_assumptions.value_used: 256 m (cross-section 4,290.6 m^2, combined with S4's real 16.76 m charted depth)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No real, citable 'array site width' exists for a fictional channel modeled on a real bay entrance that is itself ~12 miles (19 km) wide end to end (S7). 256 m is a stated scenario slice of that entrance, scaled to a plausible single-array pilot site rather than the full bay mouth, and specifically tuned (per SPEC Section 2's ~20% balance-cap guidance and FACILITATOR.md's design note) so neither channel trivially dominates on raw volume alone.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: This is the single most dilemma-relevant assumption in the case. At the real charted depth (16.76 m): a width above ~310 m widens the Reach's volume lead past SPEC's ~20% cap; a width below ~200 m flips the recommendation to the Narrows. margin_pct (9.21%) is directly and materially sensitive to this number.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Generation-potential conversion factor (kWh per m^3 of water moved through the channel cross-section, per cycle)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Derived from S5's real, published Verdant Power Gen5 KHPS array specification: 1,050 kW combined rated output at a 2.25 m/s design current speed, through a real 589.0 m^2 swept footprint. factor = 1,050 kW / (2.25 m/s x 589.0 m^2) / 3600 = 0.00022 kWh/m^3. No manufacturer or DOE/NREL report publishes a direct 'kWh per m^3' figure for any small tidal-turbine array (see not_found[]); this factor is derived from two real, cited numbers rather than invented outright, but its application to the full channel cross-section (rather than only the fraction of flow actually passing through the array's own swept footprint) is itself a disclosed scenario simplification.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Applied identically to both channels, so it does not change which channel wins the D3/D5 comparison -- that is decided entirely by channel volume (Appendix C x Appendix A/B). It scales both channels' absolute kWh figures up or down together. If a Hero argues the real capture fraction should differ by channel (e.g., because the array occupies 41% of the Narrows' cross-section but only 14% of the Reach's -- see Appendix C note), that is a legitimate, defensible challenge to this assumption's scope, not to its value.

sensitivity_note: SPEC Section 6 does not apply -- this is a siting/business decision with no death, illness, or family-hardship stakes.

balance.argument_a: The Narrows has a real, published peak current speed 3.4x the Reach's (5.28 kn vs. 1.53 kn) -- the traditional siting instinct is that peak-speed sites are always preferred for kinetic turbines, since instantaneous power scales with the cube of speed (a real fact, not modeled directly in this case's own simplified per-m3 metric).
balance.argument_b: The Reach wins on this case's actual computed primary metric. Using the full real 6-minute NOAA series for each channel (numerically integrated), the Narrows moves ~49,480,854 m^3 per cycle through its real 1,427.0 m^2 cross-section, while the Reach moves ~54,498,397 m^3 through its assumed 4,290.6 m^2 cross-section (MA1) -- the Reach's longer, flatter flow window (456 min vs. 366 min) outweighs the Narrows' much higher peak. Since Appendix D's conversion factor (MA2) is identical for both channels, this same ~9.2% volume advantage carries straight through to kWh: Narrows ~10,889 kWh/cycle vs. Reach ~11,993 kWh/cycle.
balance.margin_basis: Computed by case-research using numerical (trapezoidal) integration of each station's complete real 6-minute NOAA current-prediction series (61 points for the Narrows' 366-min ebb pulse, 77 points for the Reach's 456-min flood pulse) -- a Riemann-sum-style ground-truth calculation distinct from, and used to cross-check against, the polynomial-curve-fit-and-FTC approach a Hero will produce for Challenge D2/D3. Speed integral (m) x channel cross-sectional area (Appendix C) = volume moved (m^3) per cycle; volume x Appendix D's shared conversion factor (MA2) = total kWh per cycle. margin_pct = |Narrows_kWh - Reach_kWh| / max(Narrows_kWh, Reach_kWh) x 100. Full arithmetic in RESEARCH_LOG.md.

deliverables.text: A scatter plot of the raw current-speed readings for each channel across one full tidal cycle, time since slack water on the horizontal axis and current speed on the vertical axis, one plot per channel.

A fitted-curve worksheet for each channel: the polynomial function fit to that channel's scatter plot, and its indefinite integral (antiderivative), found term-by-term using the power rule, shown as work.

A definite-integral volume table: for each channel, the definite integral of the fitted curve over its flow window (evaluated via the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus), converted using the channel's cross-sectional area into a total volume of water moved, in cubic meters, per tidal cycle.

A Riemann-sum cross-check: for each channel, a Riemann sum built directly from the raw six-minute-interval readings (not the fitted curve) approximating the same per-cycle volume, stated side-by-side with the Challenge D3 result and a note on how closely the two methods agree.

A generation-potential ratio table: for each channel, the total per-cycle volume from D3, the channel's generation-potential ratio (kilowatt-hours per cubic meter moved), and every unit conversion used to get there, shown step by step.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: reach_width_m (MA1, 256 m) is a good-faith scenario estimate made from the closest public analogue -- S7's real ~12-mile (19 km) Chesapeake Bay entrance width, scaled down to a plausible single pilot-array-site slice, comparable in scale to real deployed tidal-array footprints (e.g., MeyGen's Inner Sound development) -- not a publicly documented single 'array site width,' since no real site at this location has been engineered, surveyed, or published. sensitivity_model.py's mechanical +/-50% sweep (2026-09-12 run) confirms this is genuinely load-bearing, not a scoping artifact: at -50% (128 m) the winner FLIPS from B (the Reach) to A (the Narrows) and the margin widens to 81.5%, breaching SPEC Section 2's 20% balance cap; at +50% (384 m) the winner stays B but the margin still widens to 65.3%, also breaching the 20% cap. Both directions breach the cap; one direction also flips the recommendation outright. This is disclosed here in full, not softened -- MA1 is the single most fragile, dilemma-relevant assumption in the case, and a Hero who challenges this specific width is raising exactly the right question. See case.json.modeling_assumptions[MA1] and FACILITATOR.md for the same finding in prose.
